item.text: {"question_id":"3B.10","answer":"The evidence does not establish that López Obrador left Mexico durably safer overall. There were mixed improvements: homicide and several urban-crime measures declined from 2018 to 2023, perceived insecurity fell, and confidence in some security institutions increased; however, the data are affected by high cifra negra, reporting and classification uncertainty, and a reversal in overall reported crime from 2022 to 2023 (BATCH-0016-E009; BATCH-0016-E012; BATCH-0021-R01-E012). In 2023, more than 30,500 people were killed, organized-crime and political violence remained severe, peace was still worse than in 2015, and reported disappearances reached 111,540 in the national registry through September, with the UN identifying inadequate investigation and almost absolute impunity (BATCH-0003-E003; BATCH-0004-E019; BATCH-0045-E002; BATCH-0045-E003). State-protection failures also persisted: arbitrary detention remained widespread; military policing was linked in the UN Working Group’s findings to violence, torture, disappearances, and homicides; prison overcrowding, violence, complaints, and weak remedies continued; and justice-system impunity remained above 90% (BATCH-0049-E011; BATCH-0016-E010). Positive measures included reforms, detention-registration infrastructure, strengthened gender-violence laws and capacities, protection and asylum-system initiatives, and some responsive displacement and victim-support actions, but their enforcement and nationwide effect are not established (BATCH-0049-E011; BATCH-0015-E016; BATCH-0015-E017). The administration’s expanded military role cannot be credited confidently for the homicide decline: subnational analysis found reductions were not consistently associated with greater National Guard activity and, in the controlled solution, absence of National Guard operations was associated with homicide reduction (BATCH-0016-E011). The inherited baseline was already extremely violent and institutionally weak; organized-crime fragmentation, external firearms supply, decentralized responsibility, and reporting suppression or self-censorship constrain causal attribution and exposure-adjusted comparison (BATCH-0003-E003; BATCH-0012-E007). Overall, the period shows mixed selected safety improvements but no demonstrated durable, ruler-attributable improvement sufficient to offset persistent severe non-state violence, state-abuse risks, and weakened accountability.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0016-E009","BATCH-0016-E012","BATCH-0021-R01-E012","BATCH-0015-E016","BATCH-0015-E017","BATCH-0049-E011"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0003-E003","BATCH-0004-E019","BATCH-0045-E002","BATCH-0045-E003","BATCH-0016-E010","BATCH-0016-E011","BATCH-0012-E007"],"limitations_and_gaps":["No complete counterfactual or exposure-adjusted national safety estimate establishes durable causal change attributable to López Obrador.","Several indicators combine federal, state, criminal, inherited, and external causes; National Guard activity was not consistently associated with subnational homicide reductions, but the analysis does not prove that it increased violence everywhere.","High cifra negra, possible undercounting or reclassification, reporting freedom, criminal threats, and self-censorship limit outcome comparability.","Some positive reforms and protection initiatives lack evidence of uniform enforcement, nationwide reach, or durable effects.","Poverty and inequality improvements were excluded as safety evidence because the supplied material does not establish a specific reduction in severe physical insecurity from those changes."],"corrections_made":["Removed poverty and inequality improvements as favorable safety outcomes absent a demonstrated physical-safety causal chain.","Added the omitted balanced evidence on reduced urban crime, lower perceived insecurity, increased institutional confidence, high cifra negra, and measurement uncertainty.","Narrowed causal claims about homicide reduction, military policy, institutional reforms, and decentralized violence.","Preserved positive protection and oversight initiatives while distinguishing formal capacity from demonstrated enforcement and remedy.","Clarified the inherited baseline, external firearms supply, organized-crime context, reporting constraints, and attribution limits."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["A full ledger review could test whether additional target-period evidence changes the balance on disappearances, civilian oversight, military abuse, or exposure-adjusted safety.","The durability comparison remains sensitive to unresolved measurement and reporting changes, especially homicide classification, cifra negra, and disappearance-record methodology."]}
